facts.text: Fort Riley was originally called Camp Center because surveyors thought it sat near the geographic center of the United States.
In 1918, Fort Riley became the first ground zero for the Spanish influenza, infecting soldiers before the pandemic spread nationwide.
The 9th and 10th Cavalry Regiments, known as Buffalo Soldiers, were stationed at Fort Riley multiple times during its history.
Camp Funston, a massive training camp built east of Fort Riley in 1917, became the site where the influenza outbreak began.
An atomic cannon sits on the hills overlooking Marshall Army Airfield, a relic of Cold War deterrence at Fort Riley.
Fort Riley’s 1st Infantry Division Museum showcases artifacts from the division’s service since 1917, including World War I and modern conflicts.
